result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say the palette works, keep all five values, and add only tints and states with no extra accents or gold. A is tighter. It also notices that a darker card surface would push Muted below 4.5:1, while B recommends exactly that darker surface (#ede6d6) after warning that Muted shouldn't sit on darker surfaces. B gives broader advice on where premium feel comes from (type, whitespace, photography), but it runs longer and adds more items. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say plainly that the palette works and keep all five values, but both then add several new colors (a surface tone, a hairline and a hover state), which makes them less proportionate than they should be. B explains better why the palette works: the green-gray ink on warm paper feels printed, and rust is the only saturated color. B also checks its additions against the existing colors, warning that a darker surface would push Muted below the contrast threshold. That flaw is in A's own #ede6d6 suggestion. A's advice on typography and photography is a useful pointer to where premium feel really comes from, but A runs a bit longer overall.
